aiOverview.content: As of late March 2026, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate is hovering around 6.22% to 6.55%, rising to its highest level in over three months due to market volatility and inflation concerns. Rates have increased from under 6% earlier in the month, with lender-specific rates (e.g., Bank of America) sometimes higher. Current 30-Year Mortgage Market (As of March 24, 2026): Average 30-Year Fixed: 6.43% – 6.55%. Freddie Mac Weekly Average: 6.22% (as of March 19). 30-Year FHA/VA: Rates for government-backed loans are generally lower, with FHA around 6.02% and VA around 6.31%. 30-Year Jumbo: 6.54% – 6.67%. Factors Influencing Rates: Market Volatility: Rates have risen following geopolitical instability, specifically conflicts causing energy price spikes and inflation fears. Weekly Increases: Rates have increased for consecutive weeks after dipping below 6% in early March. Compared to Last Year: Current rates are lower than the 6.67% average seen at this time in 2025. Note: Mortgage rates change daily. The rates above are national averages and based on top-tier credit (720+ FICO) and a 20% down payment.
